title: Restriction to an open and pullback: compatibility of the adjunction units
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $W\subseteq X$ an open subscheme and $W'=g^{-1}(W)\subseteq Y$; let $j_W:W\to X$, $j_{W'}:W'\to Y$ be the open immersions (etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]) and $g_W:W'\to W$ the restriction of $g$, so that $g\circ j_{W'}=j_W\circ g_W=:h$. Let inverse images, direct images and units of the small etale sites be as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] ($\eta_u:\mathrm{id}\to u_*u^{-1}$), where $W\times_XY$ is identified with the open subscheme $W'$ of $Y$ (and $W\times_WW'$ with $W'$) by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], so that $(g_*H)(W)=H(W')$ for an abelian sheaf $H$ on $Y_{\Et}$ and $\Gamma(W,g_{W*}H')=\Gamma(W',H')$ for one on $W'_{\Et}$. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] let $\kappa_F=c_{g,j_{W'},F}^{-1}\circ c_{j_W,g_W,F}:g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}F$, with $c$ the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (so $\kappa$ is natural in $F$), and let $\rho_F:j_W^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_W$ and $\rho_{g^{-1}F}:j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}F)|_{W'}$ be the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), so $\rho_F(W):\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(W)$ and $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W'):\Gamma(W',j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}(g^{-1}F)(W')$. Then for every $a\in\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}F)$,
$$
\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')\bigl(\kappa_F(W')\bigl(\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(W)(a)\bigr)\bigr)=\eta_{g,F}(W)\bigl(\rho_F(W)(a)\bigr)\quad\text{in }(g^{-1}F)(W'),
$$
i.e. the composite $\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\eta_{g_W}}\Gamma(W',g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\kappa_F}\Gamma(W',j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\rho}(g^{-1}F)(W')$ equals $\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\rho_F(W)}F(W)\xrightarrow{\eta_{g,F}(W)}(g^{-1}F)(W')$: under the identifications of the inverse image along an open immersion with the restriction, pulling back sections along $g_W$ is pulling back sections along $g$.

source.place: not stated in the source (agent-identified gap, needed by lem-weil-pbc-etale-mayer-vietoris-pullback step 4); the setting is that of Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03F3 (localization and restriction of sheaves). Intended proof (agent): both sides are the $W$-sections of morphisms of sheaves $j_W^{-1}F\to g_{W*}(j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}F)$ on $W_{\Et}$ (via $\rho$); by the adjunction $j_W^{-1}\dashv j_{W*}$ they agree once their composites with $\eta_{j_W,F}$ agree, and these are computed on each object $T$ of $X_{\Et}$ with the unit compatibility of $c$ ([lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2), for both factorizations of $h$), [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2) (unit = restriction, for $j_W$ and $j_{W'}$) and the naturality of $\eta_g$ along $T\times_XW\to T$: both become $F(T)\to F(T\times_XW)\to(g^{-1}F)(T\times_XW')$.

proof.text: **Step 1 (the objects over $W'$ and their identifications).** Two facts from the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]: (a) if $m:A\to C$ is a monomorphism, then for every $B\to C$ the projection $A\times_CB\to B$ is a monomorphism (two maps into $A\times_CB$ with equal second components have first components with equal composites with $m$); (b) if moreover $B\to C$ factors as $m\circ t$, the projection $A\times_CB\to B$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(t,\mathrm{id}_B)$. The open immersions $j_W$, $j_{W'}$ are monomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. The sections occurring in the proof are taken at the following schemes, read off from the formula $(u_*H)(T)=H(T\times_{\text{target}}\text{source})$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]: $P_0=W\times_XW$ (object $b_{j_W}(W)$ of $W_{\Et}$, via its second projection), $P_1=W\times_XY$ (in $(g_*H)(W)$), $P_2=W'\times_YW'$ (object $b_{j_{W'}}(W')$ of $Y_{\Et}$), $P_3=(W\times_XY)\times_YW'$ (in $(g_*j_{W'*}H)(W)$), $P_4=W\times_XW'$, fibre product of $j_W$ and $h$ (in $(h_*H)(W)$), $P_5=(W\times_XW)\times_WW'$ (in $(j_{W*}g_{W*}H)(W)$) and $P_6=W\times_WW'$ (in $\Gamma(W,g_{W*}H)$). By (b), the projection $\pi_0:P_0\to W$ is an isomorphism (both projections, being equal after composing with the monomorphism $j_W$, are equal); $\pi_1:P_1\to W'$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] fixed in the statement (so $P_1\to Y$ is $j_{W'}\circ\pi_1$, a monomorphism); and the projections $\pi_2:P_2\to W'$, $\pi_3:P_3\to W'$, $\pi_4:P_4\to W'$, $\pi_5:P_5\to W'$, $\pi_6:P_6\to W'$ are isomorphisms by (b), applied to the monomorphisms $j_{W'}$, $P_1\to Y$, $j_W$, $\mathrm{pr}_2:P_0\to W$ (an isomorphism), $\mathrm{id}_W$, through which $j_{W'}$, $j_{W'}$, $h=j_W\circ g_W$, $g_W$, $g_W$ factor. Regard each $P_k$ ($1\le k\le6$) as a $Y$-scheme via $j_{W'}\circ\pi_k$, a monomorphism. Then between two of them there is exactly one $Y$-morphism, $\pi_l^{-1}\circ\pi_k:P_k\to P_l$ (any $Y$-morphism agrees with it after composing with the monomorphism $P_l\to Y$). In particular every canonical morphism between them used below that commutes with the maps to $W'$ (hence to $Y$) — the isomorphisms $\phi:P_5\to P_4$ and $\phi':P_3\to P_4$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (1) for $(u,v)=(j_W,g_W)$ and $(g,j_{W'})$ (morphisms over $Z=W'$), and $\pi_0\times_WW':P_5\to P_6$ — is $\pi_l^{-1}\pi_k$. For a sheaf $H$ on $Y_{\Et}$ or $W'_{\Et}$ (each $P_k$ an object via $\pi_k$, isomorphic to $W'$ by $\pi_k$, a morphism of the site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]) we identify $H(P_k)$ with $H(W')$ through the bijection $H(\pi_k)$, and $F'(P_0)$ with $F'(W)$ through $F'(\pi_0)$ for a sheaf $F'$ on $W_{\Et}$ or $X_{\Et}$. These identifications are compatible with each other and with $H(\phi),H(\phi'),H(\pi_0\times_WW')$ (all are $H$ of the unique $Y$-isomorphisms), and with every morphism of sheaves $\alpha:H\to H'$ ($\alpha(P_k)\circ H(\pi_k)=H'(\pi_k)\circ\alpha(W')$, naturality). This is how the statement reads $(g^{-1}F)(W\times_XY)$ as $(g^{-1}F)(W')$ and $\Gamma(W,g_{W*}H)$ as $H(W')$; below, an equality 'under the identifications' means equality after composing with these bijections.

proof.text: **Step 2 (the units of the open immersions at $W$ and $W'$).** By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2) for $j=j_W$, $G=F$ and the object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$: $\rho_F(P_0)\circ\eta_{j_W,F}(W)=F(\pi_0):F(W)\to F(P_0)$ (the projection $P_0\to W$ is $\pi_0$, step 1). By naturality of the morphism of sheaves $\rho_F:j_W^{-1}F\to F|_W$ along the morphism $\pi_0:P_0\to W$ of $W_{\Et}$, $\rho_F(P_0)\circ(j_W^{-1}F)(\pi_0)=F|_W(\pi_0)\circ\rho_F(W)=F(\pi_0)\circ\rho_F(W)$. Since $F(\pi_0)$, $(j_W^{-1}F)(\pi_0)$ and $\rho_F(W)$ are bijective, $\eta_{j_W,F}(W)=(j_W^{-1}F)(\pi_0)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}$; under the identifications of step 1: $\eta_{j_W,F}(W)=\rho_F(W)^{-1}$ (E1). The same argument for $j=j_{W'}$, $G=g^{-1}F$ and the object $W'$ of $Y_{\Et}$ (projection $\pi_2$) gives $\eta_{j_{W'},g^{-1}F}(W')=(j_{W'}^{-1}g^{-1}F)(\pi_2)\circ\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}$, i.e. $\eta_{j_{W'},g^{-1}F}(W')=\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}$ under the identifications (E2).

proof.text: **Step 3 (the unit of $h$ through $h=j_W\circ g_W$).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) with $u=j_W$, $v=g_W$, $G=F$: $j_{W*}g_{W*}(c_{j_W,g_W,F})\circ j_{W*}(\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F})\circ\eta_{j_W,F}=d_{j_W,g_W,h^{-1}F}\circ\eta_{h,F}$. Evaluate at the object $W$ of $X_{\Et}$, using that a direct image acts on morphisms of sheaves componentwise, $(u_*\alpha)(T)=\alpha(T\times\ldots)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $d(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\phi)$ (lemma (1)): $c_{j_W,g_W,F}(P_5)\circ\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(P_0)\circ\eta_{j_W,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\phi)\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$ as maps $F(W)\to(h^{-1}F)(P_5)$. By naturality of the unit $\eta_{g_W}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] in the object, along $\pi_0:P_0\to W$ of $W_{\Et}$ (on $g_{W*}K$ this is $K(\pi_0\times_WW')$), and (E1): $\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(P_0)\circ\eta_{j_W,F}(W)=K(\pi_0\times_WW')\circ\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}$, $K=g_W^{-1}j_W^{-1}F$. Passing to $W'$ with step 1 (the morphism of sheaves $c_{j_W,g_W,F}$ commutes with the identifications, and $\pi_0\times_WW'$, $\phi$ are the unique $Y$-isomorphisms): $c_{j_W,g_W,F}(W')\circ\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}=\eta_{h,F}(W)$ as maps $F(W)\to(h^{-1}F)(W')$ (E3).

proof.text: **Step 4 (the unit of $h$ through $h=g\circ j_{W'}$).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) with $u=g$, $v=j_{W'}$, $G=F$: $g_*j_{W'*}(c_{g,j_{W'},F})\circ g_*(\eta_{j_{W'},g^{-1}F})\circ\eta_{g,F}=d_{g,j_{W'},h^{-1}F}\circ\eta_{h,F}$. At the object $W$, as in step 3: $c_{g,j_{W'},F}(P_3)\circ\eta_{j_{W'},g^{-1}F}(P_1)\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)=(h^{-1}F)(\phi')\circ\eta_{h,F}(W)$, with $\eta_{g,F}(W):F(W)\to(g^{-1}F)(P_1)$. By naturality of $\eta_{j_{W'}}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] along the isomorphism $\pi_1:P_1\to W'$ of $Y_{\Et}$ (on $j_{W'*}K'$ this is $K'(\pi_1\times_YW')$, the unique $Y$-isomorphism $P_3\to P_2$) and (E2), and with step 1: $c_{g,j_{W'},F}(W')\circ\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)=\eta_{h,F}(W)$ as maps $F(W)\to(h^{-1}F)(W')$, where $\eta_{g,F}(W)$ is read in $(g^{-1}F)(W')$ as in the statement (E4).

proof.text: **Step 5 (conclusion).** By (E3) and (E4), $c_{j_W,g_W,F}(W')\circ\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}=c_{g,j_{W'},F}(W')\circ\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)$. Apply $c_{g,j_{W'},F}(W')^{-1}$ (the component of the inverse of the isomorphism $c_{g,j_{W'}}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2)); by the definition $\kappa_F=c_{g,j_{W'},F}^{-1}\circ c_{j_W,g_W,F}$ this reads $\kappa_F(W')\circ\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)^{-1}=\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')^{-1}\circ\eta_{g,F}(W)$. Composing with $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')$ on the left and $\rho_F(W)$ on the right gives $\rho_{g^{-1}F}(W')\circ\kappa_F(W')\circ\eta_{g_W,j_W^{-1}F}(W)=\eta_{g,F}(W)\circ\rho_F(W)$, which evaluated at $a\in\Gamma(W,j_W^{-1}F)$ is the assertion.
